grov.explanation: "Grov" means "coarse", "crude" or "serious", depending on the use. For a material: "grov sand" (coarse sand). For words and jokes: "et groft sprog" (crude language). For a mistake or a crime: "en grov fejl" (a serious mistake).

sentence.da: Han fortalte en **grov** vittighed, og ingen grinede.
sentence.en: He told a rude joke, and nobody laughed.

grundig.explanation: "Grundig" means "thorough", doing or checking every part with great attention. It comes from "grund" (bottom, foundation), so a thorough person goes to the bottom of things.

sentence.da: Lægen lavede en **grundig** undersøgelse og tog mange prøver.
sentence.en: The doctor did a thorough examination and took many samples.

grundigt.explanation: "Grundigt" means "thoroughly", doing something with attention to every detail. It is the form of "grundig" (thorough) used with a verb.

sentence.da: Jeg læste kontrakten **grundigt** og fandt tre fejl.
sentence.en: I read the contract thoroughly and found three mistakes.

grundlovsdag.explanation: "Grundlovsdag" means "Constitution Day", 5 June, the day in 1849 when Denmark's first constitution was signed. It is built from grundlov (constitution) and dag (day).

sentence.da: På **grundlovsdag** holder politikere ofte taler om demokrati.
sentence.en: On Constitution Day, politicians often give speeches about democracy.

grundlæggende.explanation: "Grundlæggende" means "basic" or "fundamental", what everything else rests on. It is built from grund (foundation) and at lægge (to lay).

sentence.da: Alle mennesker har et **grundlæggende** behov for mad og vand.
sentence.en: All people have a basic need for food and water.

grå.explanation: "Grå" means "gray". It is also used for weather: "en grå dag" (a gray day) is a dull, cloudy day.

sentence.da: Himlen er **grå** og ikke blå.
sentence.en: The sky is gray and not blue.

grådig.explanation: "Grådig" means "greedy", wanting more and more, especially money or food. To name the thing you want more of, use "efter" (after): "grådig efter penge" (greedy for money).

sentence.da: Han er **grådig** og tager altid den største kage.
sentence.en: He is greedy and always takes the biggest cake.

gråvejr.explanation: "Gråvejr" means "gray weather": dull, overcast weather with a gray sky, but not necessarily rain. It is made from grå (gray) and vejr (weather).

sentence.da: Der er **gråvejr** og grå himmel.
sentence.en: It is gray weather with a gray sky.

grækenland.explanation: "Grækenland" means "Greece". It is built from græker (a Greek person) and land (country). The word "land" ends many country names: "Tyskland" (Germany) and "Irland" (Ireland).

sentence.da: Athen er en by i **Grækenland**.
sentence.en: Athens is a city in Greece.

grænseløs.explanation: "Grænseløs" means "boundless", having no limit. The ending "-løs" means "without", so "grænse" (border) plus "-løs" is "without a border". The same ending is in "hjælpeløs" (helpless).

sentence.da: Børns fantasi er **grænseløs**, og alt kan ske.
sentence.en: Children's imagination is boundless, and anything can happen.

græs.explanation: "Græs" means "grass". To mow the lawn, Danes say "at slå græs" (literally, "to hit grass").

sentence.da: Koen æder **græs** på marken.
sentence.en: The cow eats grass in the field.

græsk.explanation: "Græsk" means "Greek", for the language and for anything from that country.

sentence.da: Hun er fra Grækenland og taler **græsk**.
sentence.en: She is from Greece and speaks Greek.

grød.explanation: "En grød" means "a porridge". Add the grain in front to name the kind: "havregrød" (oat porridge).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser varm **grød** med mælk til morgenmad.
sentence.en: I eat warm porridge with milk for breakfast.

grøn.explanation: "Grøn" means "green". It also means eco-friendly: "grøn energi" (green energy). Vegetables are "grøntsager" (literally, "green things").

sentence.da: Bilen er **grøn** som græs.
sentence.en: The car is green like grass.

grønland.explanation: "Grønland" means "Greenland". It is built from grøn (green) and land (country), so literally green land. Many country names end in "land": "Tyskland" (Germany) and "Irland" (Ireland).

sentence.da: **Grønland** er en stor ø med is.
sentence.en: Greenland is a big island with ice.

grønlandsk.explanation: "Grønlandsk" means "Greenlandic", from "Grønland" (Greenland). Use it for things and for the language: "grønlandsk mad" (Greenlandic food), "Hun taler grønlandsk" (She speaks Greenlandic). Languages and nationalities are written with a lowercase letter in Danish.

sentence.da: På Grønland taler de fleste **grønlandsk**, og mange kan også dansk.
sentence.en: In Greenland, most people speak Greenlandic, and many also know Danish.

grøntsager.explanation: "Grøntsager" means "vegetables". In shops, the section is often labeled "frugt og grønt" (fruit and vegetables).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser gulerødder og andre **grøntsager**.
sentence.en: I eat carrots and other vegetables.

gudskelov.explanation: "Gudskelov" means "thank God", said with relief when something bad did not happen or a worry is over. It is short for "Gud ske lov" (God be praised).

sentence.da: **Gudskelov** kom ingen til skade i ulykken.
sentence.en: Thank God, no one was hurt in the accident.

sentence.da: Solen er **gul** og himlen blå.
sentence.en: The sun is yellow and the sky is blue.

guld.explanation: "Guld" means "gold", the metal. It can also mean something very precious: "Du er guld værd" means "You are worth your weight in gold" (literally, "You are worth gold").

sentence.da: Ringen er lavet af **guld**.
sentence.en: The ring is made of gold.

gummi.explanation: "Gummi" means "rubber", the soft material that stretches and keeps water out. It also starts the word for chewy candy: "gummibjørne" (gummy bears).

sentence.da: Støvler af **gummi** holder fødderne tørre.
sentence.en: Boots made of rubber keep your feet dry.

gylden.explanation: "Gylden" means "golden" and describes the color or the look of gold. For something made of real gold, use "guld" (gold): "en guldring" (a gold ring).

sentence.da: Solen var **gylden** over havet.
sentence.en: The sun was golden over the sea.

gyldig.explanation: "Gyldig" means "valid", accepted by the rules or still usable. To say until when, use "til" (until): "Kørekortet er gyldigt til 2030" (The driver's license is valid until 2030).

sentence.da: Billetten er **gyldig** i to timer efter købet.
sentence.en: The ticket is valid for two hours after the purchase.

gymnastik.explanation: "Gymnastik" means "gymnastics", the sport with jumps, rolls and balance work. It also means simple exercises for your body: "Jeg laver gymnastik hver morgen" (I do exercises every morning).

sentence.da: Børnene går til **gymnastik** to gange om ugen.
sentence.en: The children go to gymnastics twice a week.

gådefuld.explanation: "Gådefuld" means "mysterious", hard to understand and leaving you with questions. It is made of gåde (a riddle) and -fuld (full of), and is often used about things such as looks, smiles and people who reveal little.

sentence.da: Hendes svar var kort og **gådefuld**.
sentence.en: Her answer was short and mysterious.

gær.explanation: "Gær" means "yeast", the ingredient that makes bread rise.

sentence.da: Jeg bruger **gær**, når jeg bager brød.
sentence.en: I use yeast when I bake bread.

gødning.explanation: "En gødning" means "a fertilizer", something added to the ground so crops grow better. It can be made in a factory or come from animal manure.

sentence.da: Landmanden spreder **gødning** på marken for at hjælpe planterne.
sentence.en: The farmer spreads fertilizer on the field to help the plants.

gør det selv.explanation: "Gør det selv" means "do it yourself". It is made of gør (do), det (it) and selv (yourself). "Selv" stays the same for every person: "Han gør det selv" (He does it himself) and "Vi gør det selv" (We do it ourselves).

sentence.da: Jeg hjælper dig ikke. **Gør det selv**!
sentence.en: I will not help you. Do it yourself!

at hacke.explanation: "At hacke" means "to hack", to break into a computer, an account or a network without permission. Do not mix it up with "at hakke" (to chop), which has kk and is used for cutting or digging.

sentence.da: Nogen forsøgte at **hacke** firmaets netværk i går nat.
sentence.en: Someone tried to hack the company's network last night.

at hade.explanation: "At hade" means "to hate", and it is a strong word. For everyday dislikes, Danes often say something milder, such as "Jeg kan ikke lide" (I don't like).

sentence.da: Man skal ikke **hade** andre.
sentence.en: You should not hate others.

at hagle.explanation: "At hagle" means "to hail", for ice falling from the sky as small hard balls: "Det hagler" (It is hailing). Like "det regner" (it is raining) and "det sner" (it is snowing), it starts with "det" (it).

sentence.da: Det begynder at **hagle** med store, hårde isklumper.
sentence.en: It starts to hail with big, hard lumps of ice.

at hakke.explanation: "At hakke" means "to chop" or "to mince", cutting something into small pieces. Ground meat is "hakket kød" (chopped meat).

sentence.da: Man kan **hakke** persille med en skarp kniv.
sentence.en: You can chop parsley with a sharp knife.

at halte.explanation: "At halte" means "to limp", to walk unevenly because a leg or foot hurts. You can use it for a weak argument too: "Argumentet halter" (The argument is weak).

sentence.da: Han vil **halte** i flere uger, fordi hans fod er brækket.
sentence.en: He will limp for several weeks because his foot is broken.

at halvere.explanation: "At halvere" means "to halve", to cut an amount to half of what it was, or to split something into two equal parts.

sentence.da: Butikken vil **halvere** prisen på alle varer.
sentence.en: The store will halve the price of all goods.

at handle.explanation: "At handle" means "to shop", buying things in stores: "Jeg handler i supermarkedet" (I shop at the supermarket). For food, Danes say "at handle ind" (to do the grocery shopping). With "om" (about) it means "to be about": "Filmen handler om kærlighed" (The film is about love).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **handle** i den nye butik.
sentence.en: I want to shop in the new store.

at handle ind.explanation: "At handle ind" means "to go grocery shopping", for food and everyday items. For clothes, say "at shoppe" (to shop).

sentence.da: Vi skal **handle ind**, fordi der ikke er mælk.
sentence.en: We have to go grocery shopping because there is no milk.

at handle om.explanation: "At handle om" means "to be about", for the topic of a book, film or talk: "Filmen handler om en hund" (The film is about a dog). Do not mix it up with "at handle" (to shop): "Jeg handler i supermarkedet" (I shop at the supermarket).

sentence.da: Min bog skal **handle om** en hund.
sentence.en: My book is going to be about a dog.

at harmonere.explanation: "At harmonere" means "to harmonize": to fit well together so that nothing feels out of place, for example colors, sounds or ideas. Add "med" (with) to say with what: "Gardinerne harmonerer med væggene" (The curtains go well with the walls).

sentence.da: Gule og blå farver kan **harmonere** godt.
sentence.en: Yellow and blue colors can harmonize well.

at have.explanation: "At have" means "to have" or "to own". You also use "har" (have) with another verb to talk about the past: "Jeg har spist" (I have eaten). Danes say "Jeg har fødselsdag" (It is my birthday; literally, "I have birthday") where English uses "to be".

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **have** en kop kaffe.
sentence.en: I would like to have a cup of coffee.

at have ansvar for.explanation: "At have ansvar for" means "to be responsible for". "Ansvar" means "responsibility", so it is literally "to have responsibility for".

sentence.da: Læreren skal **have ansvar for** klassen.
sentence.en: The teacher has to be responsible for the class.

at have brug for.explanation: "At have brug for" means "to need". Literally, it is "to have use for". Another way to say it is "at behøve" (to need), which is often used with "ikke" (not): "Du behøver ikke at komme" (You do not need to come).

sentence.da: Man kan **have brug for** en paraply.
sentence.en: You may need an umbrella.

at have det sjovt.explanation: "At have det sjovt" means "to have fun". The part "have det" (to feel) works with other feelings too: "Jeg har det godt" (I feel good).

sentence.da: Vi vil **have det sjovt** i weekenden.
sentence.en: We want to have fun this weekend.

at have en finger med i spillet.explanation: "At have en finger med i spillet" means "to be involved in something": to be one of the people responsible for what happened, often in a hidden way. Literally, it is "to have a finger in the game".

forms.da: Han har en finger med i spillet
Hun havde en finger med i spillet
forms.en: She had a hand in it

forms.da: Har du en finger med i spillet?

sentence.da: Politiet tror, at flere kan **have en finger med i spillet**.
sentence.en: The police think that several people may be involved.

at have en høne at plukke med nogen.explanation: "At have en høne at plukke med nogen" means "to have a bone to pick with someone": to be upset with a person and want to talk about the problem. Literally, it is "to have a hen to pluck with someone". To name the person you are upset with, end with "med" (with) and that person: "Jeg har en høne at plukke med dig" (I have a bone to pick with you).

forms.da: Jeg har en høne at plukke med dig
forms.en: I have a bone to pick with you

forms.da: Har du en høne at plukke med ham?
forms.en: Do you have a bone to pick with him?

forms.da: Hun havde en høne at plukke med sin bror
forms.en: She had a bone to pick with her brother

sentence.da: Det er svært at **have en høne at plukke med nogen**, man holder af.
sentence.en: It is hard to have a bone to pick with someone you love.

at have fri.explanation: "At have fri" means "to be off", with no work or school that day: "Børnene har fri i dag" (The children are off today). To choose to take a day off, say "at holde fri" (to take time off).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **have fri** på mandag.
sentence.en: I would like to have Monday off.

at have fødselsdag.explanation: "At have fødselsdag" means "to have a birthday", and it is how you say it is your birthday: "Jeg har fødselsdag i dag" (It is my birthday today). To congratulate someone, say "Tillykke med fødselsdagen!" (Happy birthday!).

sentence.da: Min bror skal **have fødselsdag** i morgen.
sentence.en: My brother has his birthday tomorrow.

at have god tid.explanation: "At have god tid" means "to have plenty of time", with no pressure. If you are in a hurry, say "at have travlt" (to be in a hurry).

forms.en: I have had plenty of time

sentence.da: Vi skal tage afsted tidligt for at **have god tid**.
sentence.en: We have to leave early to have plenty of time.

at have hjertet på rette sted.explanation: "At have hjertet på rette sted" means "to have one's heart in the right place", to have good intentions. People say it about someone who makes a mistake or acts clumsily, to show they do not hold it against them.

forms.da: Han har hjertet på rette sted.
forms.en: He has his heart in the right place.

forms.da: Hun er klodset, men hun har hjertet på rette sted.
forms.en: She is clumsy, but her heart is in the right place.

forms.da: Jeg ved, at du har hjertet på rette sted.
forms.en: I know your heart is in the right place.

sentence.da: Det er vigtigt at **have hjertet på rette sted**, når man hjælper andre.
sentence.en: It is important to have your heart in the right place when you help others.

at have is i maven.explanation: "At have is i maven" means "to keep cool" or "to stay calm": to not hurry or panic when others are nervous, for example before a deadline or a hard match. Literally, it is "to have ice in the stomach". It is often said as advice: "Man skal have is i maven" (You have to keep your cool).

sentence.da: Før eksamen er det vigtigt at **have is i maven**.
sentence.en: Before the exam it is important to keep your cool.

at have let ved.explanation: "At have let ved" means "to find it easy to". To name the activity you find easy, add "at" (to) and a verb after "ved" (at): "Jeg har let ved at lære sprog" (I find it easy to learn languages). For the opposite meaning, say "at have svært ved" (to find it hard to).

forms.en: I have found it easy to

sentence.da: Han kan **have let ved** at tegne, fordi han øver sig meget.
sentence.en: He can find it easy to draw because he practices a lot.

at have lyst til.explanation: "At have lyst til" means "to feel like", or "to want to". To name the thing you feel like having, put it after "til" (for): "Jeg har lyst til kaffe" (I feel like coffee). To name the activity you feel like doing, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Jeg har lyst til at gå en tur" (I feel like going for a walk).

forms.en: I have felt like / wanted to

sentence.da: Man kan **have lyst til** en kold drink, når det er varmt.
sentence.en: You can feel like a cold drink when it is hot.

at have mulighed for.explanation: "At have mulighed for" means "to have the opportunity to", so to be able to do something when the chance is there. For a simple "can", use "kan" (can): "Jeg kan komme" (I can come).

forms.en: I have had the opportunity to

sentence.da: Du skal **have mulighed for** at tale med chefen.
sentence.en: You should have the chance to talk to the boss.

at have noget imod.explanation: "At have noget imod" means "to mind" or "to object to". It is mostly used in questions and with "ikke" (not): "Har du noget imod musik?" (Do you mind music?) "Jeg har ikke noget imod det" (I do not mind that).

sentence.da: Jeg ville ikke **have noget imod** en kop te.
sentence.en: I would not mind a cup of tea.

at have ondt i.explanation: "At have ondt i" means "to have a pain in", for saying that a body part hurts: "Jeg har ondt i hovedet" (I have a headache) or "ondt i maven" (a stomach ache). Danish says "hovedet" (the head) where English says "my head".

forms.en: I have had a pain in

sentence.da: Efter koncerten kan man **have ondt i** halsen.
sentence.en: After the concert, you can have a sore throat.

at have på.explanation: "At have på" means "to wear", literally "to have on". Putting clothes on is a different phrase, "at tage tøj på" (literally, "to take clothes on"), and taking them off is "at tage tøj af" (to take clothes off).

sentence.da: Hvad skal du **have på** i aften?
sentence.en: What are you going to wear tonight?

at have ret.explanation: "At have ret" means "to be right". Literally, Danish says "to have right": "Du har ret" means "You are right". Do not say "Du er ret" (with "er", meaning "are") for this.

sentence.da: Ja, du kan **have ret** i det.
sentence.en: Yes, you may be right about that.

at have råd til.explanation: "At have råd til" means "to afford": "Jeg har ikke råd til en ny telefon" (I cannot afford a new phone). Here "råd" means "money to spend". Do not mix it up with "et råd" (a piece of advice): "Jeg giver dig et råd" (I give you a piece of advice).

forms.en: I have been able to afford

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **have råd til** en ny cykel.
sentence.en: I would like to be able to afford a new bike.

at have svært ved.explanation: "At have svært ved" means "to find it hard to". To name the activity you find hard, add "at" (to) and a verb after "ved" (at): "Jeg har svært ved at sove" (I find it hard to sleep). You can also name a school subject directly after "ved": "Hun har svært ved matematik" (She finds math hard).

forms.en: I have found it hard to

sentence.da: Jeg kan **have svært ved** at stå tidligt op.
sentence.en: I can find it hard to get up early.

at have tid til.explanation: "At have tid til" means "to have time for" something: "Har du tid til en kop kaffe?" (Do you have time for a cup of coffee?) To name the activity you have time to do, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Jeg har tid til at læse" (I have time to read).

sentence.da: Efter arbejde vil jeg **have tid til** børnene.
sentence.en: After work, I want to have time for the children.

at have travlt.explanation: "At have travlt" means "to be busy" or "to be in a hurry": "Jeg har travlt" (I am busy; literally, "I have busy").

sentence.da: Før jul kan butikkerne **have travlt**.
sentence.en: Before Christmas the stores can be busy.

at havne.explanation: "At havne" means "to end up", to come to rest in a place or situation, often one that was not planned: "Bolden havnede i søen" (The ball ended up in the lake). It comes from "en havn" (a harbor), the place where ships finally come in.

sentence.da: Pakken kan **havne** hos naboen, hvis vi ikke er hjemme.
sentence.en: The package may end up at the neighbor's if we are not home.

at hedde.explanation: "At hedde" means "to be called", and it is how you give your name: "Jeg hedder Anna" means "My name is Anna". It is also used for things: "Hvad hedder det på dansk?" (What is that called in Danish?).

sentence.da: Vores nye hund skal **hedde** Max.
sentence.en: Our new dog is going to be called Max.

at helbrede.explanation: "At helbrede" means "to cure", to make a sick person well or to make an illness go away. Someone or something does it, such as a doctor or a medicine. When a cut closes by itself, use "at hele" (to heal) instead.

sentence.da: Man kan **helbrede** nogle sygdomme med den rigtige behandling.
sentence.en: Some illnesses can be cured with the right treatment.

at hele.explanation: "At hele" means "to heal": a cut or a hurt feeling gets better by itself over time. When a doctor makes someone well, you say "at helbrede" (to cure).

sentence.da: Et brækket ben kan **hele** på seks uger.
sentence.en: A broken leg can heal in six weeks.

at henrette.explanation: "At henrette" means "to execute": to end someone's life as an official punishment. For any other killing, use "at dræbe" (to kill): "Han dræbte en mand" (He killed a man).

sentence.da: I nogle lande kan staten stadig **henrette** forbrydere.
sentence.en: In some countries the state can still execute criminals.

at hente.explanation: "At hente" means "to fetch" or "to pick up": you go somewhere and get a thing or a person who is waiting for you. To get something that is simply given to you, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg får en gave" (I get a present).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **hente** børnene i skolen klokken tre.
sentence.en: I have to pick up the children at school at three o'clock.

at henvende sig.explanation: "At henvende sig" means "to contact" or "to turn to", to go to a person or office to request help or information. The command form is common on signs: "Henvend dig i receptionen" (Please go to the reception desk). To name the person or office you turned to, add "til" (to) before that person or office: "Jeg henvendte mig til kommunen" (I contacted the municipality).

sentence.da: Man kan **henvende sig** til biblioteket, hvis man har spørgsmål.
sentence.en: You can turn to the library if you have questions.

at henvise.explanation: "At henvise" means "to refer", to send someone on to another person or place, with "til" (to) after it. In a text it means to point to a source: "Teksten henviser til en bog" (The text refers to a book).

sentence.da: Lægen vil **henvise** mig til en specialist på sygehuset.
sentence.en: The doctor will refer me to a specialist at the hospital.

at heppe.explanation: "At heppe" means "to cheer (for a team)", to shout and encourage a team or a person. Use "på" (for) after it: "Vi hepper på Danmark" (We are cheering for Denmark).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **heppe** på dig, når du løber maraton.
sentence.en: I will cheer for you when you run the marathon.

at hikke.explanation: "At hikke" means "to hiccup", to make a quick, small sound in your throat that you cannot control. The sound itself is "et hik" (a hiccup).

sentence.da: Man begynder at **hikke**, når man drikker for hurtigt.
sentence.en: You start to hiccup when you drink too fast.

at hilse.explanation: "At hilse" means "to greet" or "to say hello". To greet a person, add "på" (on): "Jeg hilser på naboen" (I say hello to the neighbor). "Hils ham fra mig!" (Say hi to him from me!)

sentence.da: Man skal **hilse**, når man kommer ind i butikken.
sentence.en: You should say hello when you walk into the store.

at hilse på.explanation: "At hilse på" means "to say hello to", and is used when you are introduced to someone: "Jeg vil gerne hilse på din mor" (I would like to say hello to your mom).

forms.en: I have said hello to / met

sentence.da: Du skal **hilse på** gæsterne, når de kommer.
sentence.en: You have to greet the guests when they arrive.

at hindre.explanation: "At hindre" means "to prevent" or "to hinder", to keep an event from happening or a person from doing something. To name the action that is prevented, use "i at" (from) and a verb: "Sneen hindrede os i at køre" (The snow kept us from driving).

sentence.da: Et væltet træ kan **hindre** trafikken på landevejen.
sentence.en: A fallen tree can hinder traffic on the country road.

at hive.explanation: "At hive" means "to pull" or "to heave", to pull something up or toward you with a quick, strong movement. "At hive i" means "to tug at" something, and "at hive efter vejret" means "to gasp for breath".

sentence.da: Fiskeren skal **hive** nettet op af vandet med begge hænder.
sentence.en: The fisherman has to pull the net out of the water with both hands.

at hjælpe.explanation: "At hjælpe" means "to help", making something easier for someone. Shop staff often ask "Kan jeg hjælpe dig?" (Can I help you?). "Hjælp!" (Help!) is what you call out in an emergency.

sentence.da: Lægen vil **hjælpe** den syge mand.
sentence.en: The doctor wants to help the sick man.

at hjælpe med.explanation: "At hjælpe med" means "to help with" a task. To name the task, put it after "med" (with): "hjælpe med lektierne" (help with the homework). To name the person you help, put that person before "med": "Jeg hjælper dig med maden" (I help you with the food).

sentence.da: Min bror vil **hjælpe med** flytningen.
sentence.en: My brother wants to help with the move.

at hjælpe til.explanation: "At hjælpe til" means "to help out": "Børnene hjælper til ved festen" (The kids help out at the party). You do not say whom you help. For a person, say "Jeg hjælper min mor" (I help my mom).

sentence.da: Vil du **hjælpe til** i køkkenet i aften?
sentence.en: Do you want to help out in the kitchen tonight?

at holde.explanation: "At holde" means "to hold" or "to keep": you have something in your hands, or you do not give it up. "Hun holder en kop kaffe" (She is holding a cup of coffee). "Du må holde den" (You can keep it). "Holde en fest" means "to throw a party".

sentence.da: Kan du **holde** min taske et øjeblik?
sentence.en: Can you hold my bag for a moment?

at holde af.explanation: "At holde af" means "to be fond of", a warm and gentle feeling for a person or thing. Name the person or thing after "af" (of): "Jeg holder meget af min bedstemor" (I am very fond of my grandmother).

sentence.da: Man kan **holde af** en ven uden at elske ham.
sentence.en: You can be fond of a friend without loving him.

at holde et løfte.explanation: "At holde et løfte" means "to keep a promise". The opposite is "at bryde et løfte" (to break a promise). Danish uses "holde" (to hold) where English says "keep".

sentence.da: Man skal altid **holde et løfte**.
sentence.en: You must always keep a promise.

at holde fast.explanation: "At holde fast" means "to hold on", gripping tightly: "Hold fast i rælingen!" (Hold on to the railing!) It works for ideas too: "Han holder fast i sin mening" (He sticks to his opinion).

sentence.da: Du skal **holde fast**, når bussen kører.
sentence.en: You must hold on when the bus is moving.

at holde ferie.explanation: "At holde ferie" means "to be on vacation", a longer break from work or school. For just one day off, use "at tage fri" (to take a day off).

sentence.da: Vi vil **holde ferie** ved havet i år.
sentence.en: We want to be on vacation by the sea this year.

at holde fest.explanation: "At holde fest" means "to throw a party". To go to one, say "at tage til fest" (to go to a party): "Han tager til fest" (He is going to a party).

sentence.da: Vi vil **holde fest** i haven på lørdag.
sentence.en: We want to throw a party in the garden on Saturday.

at holde fri.explanation: "At holde fri" means "to take time off", as a choice you make. To simply be off, say "at have fri" (to be off work).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **holde fri**, fordi jeg skal til lægen.
sentence.en: I want to take time off because I am going to the doctor.

at holde i hånd.explanation: "At holde i hånd" means "to hold hands". Danish literally says "i hånd" (in hand), with just one "hånd" (hand), even though two people are involved.

sentence.da: Børnene skal **holde i hånd**, når de krydser vejen.
sentence.en: The children must hold hands when they cross the road.

at holde med.explanation: "At holde med" means "to support" a team or side, meaning you want it to win: "Hvem holder du med?" (Who do you support?)

sentence.da: Jeg plejer at **holde med** det danske hold.
sentence.en: I usually support the Danish team.

at holde møde.explanation: "At holde møde" means "to have a meeting". Danish uses "holde" (to hold) here, just as English says "hold a meeting".

sentence.da: Vi skal **holde møde** i morgen tidlig.
sentence.en: We are having a meeting tomorrow morning.

at holde op.explanation: "At holde op" means "to stop", for ending an activity. To name the activity that stopped, add "med at" (with to) and a verb: "Hun holdt op med at synge" (She stopped singing).

sentence.da: Musikken skal **holde op** klokken ti.
sentence.en: The music has to stop at ten o'clock.

at holde op med.explanation: "At holde op med" means "to stop doing". Without "med" (with), "holde op" means "to stop": "Regnen holder op" (The rain stops).

sentence.da: Du skal **holde op med** at råbe.
sentence.en: You have to stop yelling.

at holde oplæg.explanation: "At holde oplæg" means "to give a presentation", to speak to a group about a topic, for example at work or in class. Danish uses "holde" (to hold) where English says "give", so the same verb works for other talks: "at holde en tale" (to give a speech).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **holde oplæg** om mit projekt for hele klassen.
sentence.en: I am going to give a presentation about my project to the whole class.

at holde ord.explanation: "At holde ord" means "to keep one's word", to do what you promised. Danish uses no word for "his" or "her" here: "Hun holder altid ord" (She always keeps her word).

sentence.da: Når du har lovet noget, skal du **holde ord**.
sentence.en: When you have promised something, you must keep your word.

at holde pause.explanation: "At holde pause" means "to take a break". Another way to say it is "at tage en pause" (to take a break): "Jeg tager en pause" (I am taking a break).

sentence.da: Vi skal **holde pause**, fordi vi er trætte.
sentence.en: We have to take a break because we are tired.

at holde sammen.explanation: "At holde sammen" means "to stick together": "Familien holder sammen" (The family sticks together). It works for things that stay in one piece too: "Kagen holder ikke sammen" (The cake does not hold together).

sentence.da: I svære tider skal vi **holde sammen**.
sentence.en: In hard times, we must stick together.

at holde sig.explanation: "At holde sig" means "to keep" or "to stay" in a place or a state: "Hold dig væk!" (Stay away!). It also goes with a state, such as "at holde sig varm" (to keep warm).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **holde sig** væk fra ilden.
sentence.en: The children must stay away from the fire.

at holde sig i form.explanation: "At holde sig i form" means "to stay in shape". "Sig" (oneself) changes with the person: "Du holder dig i form" (You stay in shape).

forms.da: jeg har holdt mig i form

sentence.da: Man skal **holde sig i form**, når man bliver ældre.
sentence.en: You have to stay in shape as you get older.

at holde styr på.explanation: "At holde styr på" means "to keep track of", so nothing gets lost or mixed up. To watch over someone, use "at holde øje med" (to keep an eye on).

sentence.da: Det er svært at **holde styr på** alle børnene.
sentence.en: It is hard to keep track of all the kids.

at holde tale.explanation: "At holde tale" means "to give a speech". Danish uses "holde" (to hold) for speeches.

sentence.da: Min chef vil **holde tale** ved festen.
sentence.en: My boss wants to give a speech at the party.

at holde tand for tunge.explanation: "At holde tand for tunge" means "to keep quiet": to say nothing about something, for example a surprise or a harsh remark. Literally, it is "to hold tooth before tongue", as if a tooth stops the tongue from speaking.

sentence.da: Du må **holde tand for tunge** og ikke sige noget om gaven.
sentence.en: You must keep quiet and not say anything about the present.

at holde øje med.explanation: "At holde øje med" means "to keep an eye on", watching over someone or something.

forms.en: I have kept an eye on

sentence.da: Kan du **holde øje med** min taske?
sentence.en: Can you keep an eye on my bag?

at hoppe.explanation: "At hoppe" means "to jump", for example into water, over a puddle or on a trampoline. Add a small word to show the direction: "hoppe op" (jump up), "hoppe ned" (jump down) and "hoppe i" (jump in).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **hoppe** i vandet.
sentence.en: The children want to jump into the water.
